walkthroughs.body_html:
Atomic Structure HL — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atomic Structure HL brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atomic Structure HL.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Aston
Mendeleev
Pauling

mcqs.q: At which electrode are positive ions reduced during electrolysis?
options: At the cathode (the negative electrode) — positive ions gain electrons there.
Positive ions are reduced at the anode because that's where positive things go.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.

mcqs.q: Why does water have a bent shape rather than linear?
options: Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
Water is bent because the hydrogens repel each other and push apart.
Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral electron geometry but a bent molecular shape.

mcqs.q: Does a catalyst affect the position of equilibrium?
options: A catalyst increases the yield by being consumed in the forward reaction only.
A catalyst shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
Positive ions are oxidised at the cathode by losing protons.
No — it speeds up both the forward and reverse reactions equally, so equilibrium is reached faster but at the same position.
